messages.subject: Re: Milkweed seeds
messages.text:
Hi Kevin,

Sorry for the long delay getting back to you, this stretched out far longer than it should have.

For spring planting, yes, stratification is needed. Our regular seed packets aren't pre-stratified, so you'll want to do a cold stratification for about 30 days before sowing: wrap the seeds in a slightly damp paper towel, seal them in a bag, and leave them in the fridge. After that, they're ready to go in the ground.

If you'd rather skip that step, we also carry seeds that come already cold-stratified and ready to sow directly, you can find them here: https://lasclay.com/en/products/graines-semences-asclepiade-stratifiees-froid

For fall planting, no stratification needed at all, winter takes care of it naturally.

Hope your planting goes well this season.

Warmly,
__
 Gabriel Gouveia 
Co-founder
Lasclay.com
